about: The interior of the prostate and the structures joined to it in this model: the capsule, the peripheral, central and transition zones, the prostatic urethra, the seminal colliculus, the two ejaculatory ducts, the seminal vesicles and the ampullae of the vas deferens. The anterior fibromuscular stroma, the gland's ducts and cells, the nerves, the venous plexus and the external sphincter are left out. The zone boundaries are smooth shapes chosen to show each zone's usual place and relative size, and the seminal vesicle's folded tube is drawn as one coil.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Prostatic Capsule
parts.summary: The fibrous and muscular covering of the gland
parts.function: The prostate is surrounded by a capsule of fibrous tissue and smooth muscle. It is drawn here as glass so that the zones, the urethra and the ducts inside it can be seen through it.

parts.label: Peripheral Zone
parts.summary: The largest zone, forming the back and sides of the gland
parts.function: The peripheral zone makes up most of the glandular tissue and lies behind and to the sides of the urethra. Its glands secrete the prostatic fluid, a thin alkaline fluid that forms part of the semen and helps sperm survive in the acid of the vagina. The gland depends on testosterone for its growth and function, so the zone brightens as testosterone rises.

drives.note: The prostate is an androgen-dependent gland.
The prostatic smooth muscle and glands empty into the urethra under sympathetic drive at emission.

parts.label: Central Zone
parts.summary: A wedge at the base of the gland, pierced by the ejaculatory ducts
parts.function: The central zone is a wedge of tissue at the base of the gland, behind the first part of the urethra, and the two ejaculatory ducts pass through it. It is drawn as glass so the ducts can be seen inside it.

parts.label: Transition Zone
parts.summary: Two small lobes lying against the urethra
parts.function: The transition zone consists of two small lobes that lie on either side of the urethra, just below the bladder. It is a small part of the gland in a young adult, and it continues to grow slowly through life.

drives.note: Growth of the gland depends on androgens.

parts.label: Prostatic Urethra
parts.summary: The part of the urethra that runs through the gland
parts.function: The urethra leaves the bladder and passes through the prostate from top to bottom, with a gentle forward curve. Urine passes along it when the bladder empties, and at ejaculation the semen is added to it from the ejaculatory ducts and the prostatic ducts. It is drawn as glass so that the streams inside it can be seen.

drives.note: Semen enters the urethra at emission.

parts.label: Seminal Colliculus
parts.summary: The small mound on the back wall of the urethra where the ducts open
parts.function: The seminal colliculus is a small rounded elevation on the back wall of the prostatic urethra. The two ejaculatory ducts open on either side of its summit, so sperm and seminal fluid enter the urethra here.

drives.note: The ducts discharge onto it during emission.

parts.label: Ejaculatory Ducts
parts.summary: The two short ducts that carry sperm and seminal fluid into the urethra
parts.function: Each ejaculatory duct is formed where the duct of a seminal vesicle joins the end of a vas deferens. It runs forward and downward through the central zone to open into the urethra at the seminal colliculus. During emission, sympathetic nerves cause the muscle of the vas, the vesicles and the prostate to contract and drive the contents along. The stream of particles in the ducts is drawn only during orgasm.

drives.note: Emission through the ducts takes place at orgasm.
Emission is triggered by sympathetic nerves.

parts.label: Seminal Vesicles
parts.summary: Two glandular sacs behind the bladder that add fluid to the semen
parts.function: The seminal vesicles are a pair of folded, coiled glandular tubes lying behind the bladder, above the prostate. They secrete a thick fluid, rich in fructose, that makes up much of the volume of the semen and nourishes the sperm. The sacs are drawn as glass, with the coiled tube inside each, and they brighten during emission.

drives.note: Their muscle contracts and empties them at emission.

parts.label: Seminal Vesicle Tubes
parts.summary: The coiled tube inside each seminal vesicle
parts.function: Each seminal vesicle is really a single long tube, folded on itself and held together by connective tissue, which is why it looks like a sac. Its lining secretes the seminal fluid, and the tube ends in a short duct that joins the vas deferens to form the ejaculatory duct.

parts.label: Ampullae of the Vas Deferens
parts.summary: The widened ends of the two vasa deferentia beside the vesicles
parts.function: Near the prostate each vas deferens widens into an ampulla that lies against the seminal vesicle. Sperm collect here before emission. The ampulla narrows again and joins the duct of the vesicle to make the ejaculatory duct.

drives.note: Emission moves sperm on from the ampullae.
